name: Police

levels.note: 10th pass. Age 18–25. Physical: running 1.6km in 6 min, long jump, high jump, chest.
12th pass. Age 18–25. Physical standards + written exam.
Any degree. Age 20–28 (SI), 21–30 (Dy.SP). Physical + written + interview.

stages.name: Physical Efficiency Test (PET)
stages.tests: Running: 1.6km (men) / 800m (women) in time limit. Long jump, high jump.
stages.note: Qualifying. 5–10% pass. Start running 3 months before.

stages.name: Physical Standard Test (PST)
stages.note: Strict measurement. No relaxation except for specific categories.

stages.name: Written Exam
stages.tests: 100-200 Qs. GK, Reasoning, Numerical Ability, General Hindi/English.
stages.note: Merit prepared from written score. Negative marking 0.25-0.50.

stages.name: Interview / Document Verification
stages.tests: Personal interview (for SI/Dy.SP). All originals, caste, domicile.
stages.note: Final appointment after medical fitness (vision, hearing, BMI).

syllabus.pattern: 80 questions, 160 marks, 60 minutes: General Intelligence & Reasoning 20, General Knowledge & General Awareness 20, Elementary Mathematics 20, English/Hindi 20. Negative 0.25. Followed by PET/PST and medical.

topics.items: Analogies, similarities and differences, spatial visualisation, spatial orientation, visual memory, observation, relationship concepts, arithmetical reasoning, figural classification, arithmetic number series, non-verbal series, coding-decoding, statement-conclusion
Current events, India and its neighbours, sports, history, culture, geography, economic scene, polity, scientific research
Number system, whole numbers, decimals and fractions, LCM and HCF, ratio and proportion, percentage, average, profit and loss, discount, mensuration, time and distance, time and work, simple interest
Grammar, vocabulary, sentence structure, synonyms and antonyms, error spotting, comprehension

syllabus.books: Police Constable Guide (Amazon) · Flipkart

syllabus.pattern: Most state boards use a 100-mark objective paper on reasoning, general studies, mathematics and the state language, followed by a physical efficiency test. Exact marks and negative marking are set by each state board.

topics.items: Indian polity and constitution, history, geography, economy, science, current affairs, and state-specific general knowledge which carries heavy weight
Series, analogy, coding-decoding, direction, blood relations, percentage, ratio, average, time-work, mensuration

topics.group: Law awareness (SI and some constable papers)
topics.items: Indian Penal Code basics, CrPC basics, Evidence Act basics, police procedures and human rights

syllabus.pattern: Typical state standard: 1.6 km run for men and 800 m for women within a fixed time, long jump and high jump, plus height, chest and eyesight standards. Qualifying — but it decides the final list in many states.

topics.items: Endurance (run), explosive strength (long and high jump), and body measurements. Standards differ by state and by category — check your state notification

syllabus.pattern: Paper I 250 marks, 2 hours, objective: general ability and intelligence. Paper II 200 marks, 3 hours, descriptive: essay, precis and report writing. Then PET/PST, medical and interview.

topics.items: General mental ability, general science, current events, Indian polity and economy, history, geography, security and law
Essay, precis writing, report writing, grammar and comprehension

reality: Police recruitment is state-specific. Each state has its own exam, syllabus, and physical standards.
Physical test eliminates 80-90% of candidates. Fitness is more important than book knowledge.
Constable has no interview — pure merit (written + physical). SI/Dy.SP have interview.
Medical standards are strict. Flat feet, knock knees, colour blindness = rejection.
Working hours are long and irregular. Night shifts, emergencies, transfers to remote areas.
Salary: Constable ~₹21,700 (Level 3) + DA + HRA. SI ~₹35,400 (Level 6) + allowances.

faq.q: What is the difference between Constable and Sub-Inspector?
faq.a: Constable: 10th pass, Level 3, beat policing. Sub-Inspector: graduate, Level 6, station house officer with investigation powers. Different exams, different eligibility.

faq.q: Can women apply for police jobs?
faq.a: Yes. Women can apply for Constable, Head Constable, SI, and Dy.SP. Separate physical standards for women (lower height, different running distance).

faq.q: What is the age limit for police recruitment?
faq.a: Constable: 18-25 years. Head Constable: 18-25. SI: 20-28 years. Dy.SP: 21-30 years. Age relaxations for SC/ST/OBC/PwD.

faq.q: Is there negative marking in police exams?
faq.a: Yes. Most state police exams have 0.25-0.50 negative marking per wrong answer. No negative marking in physical tests.

faq.q: How many vacancies are there in police recruitment?
faq.a: UP Police: 50,000+ (2024). Bihar Police: 20,000+. Total state police vacancies exceed 2 lakh per year across India.

faq.q: Where do I find official police notifications?
faq.a: State police websites (e.g., uppbpb.gov.in, csbc.bih.nic.in). SarkariJobs+ links the official notification on every listing page.

prepPlan.what: Start the run, long jump and high jump on day one, not after the written result. Physical tests are qualifying but in many states they also decide the final merit, and fitness cannot be built in a month.

Mathematics and reasoning at Class 10 level plus one general studies book. State police papers are easier than SSC but test state-specific GK heavily — get the state board's own syllabus and previous papers.
Solve the last 5–10 years of the state constable paper and SSC GD papers. Note repeated questions on state history, festivals, districts and police-related law.
Weekly full mocks with the negative-marking rule practised (skip only when you cannot eliminate two options). Check eyesight, height, chest and tattoo rules now — they are absolute disqualifications.
Alternate written revision with physical practice. Run at the same time of day as the PET slot, and do two full timed runs a week to know your pace.
